_comment: Task suite for the Claude Code OpenTelemetry capture.
Every task runs against the sandbox workspace that run_suite.py creates, never
against a real project, so the capture contains no private content and the suite
is reproducible by anyone with the repository.
'shape' records the control-flow structure the task is designed to elicit, so a
claim about concurrency in the resulting log can be checked against intent:
linear  one agent, a sequence of tool calls
chain   sub-agents spawned one after another, each using the previous result
fanout  several sub-agents spawned in one turn, running concurrently
mixed   a fan-out followed by a dependent step

tasks.prompt: List every file in the current directory with its line count, then write the result as a markdown table to inventory.md. Do not use sub-agents.
Run `python calc.py` in the current directory. It fails. Find the bug, fix it, and run it again to confirm. Do not use sub-agents.
Write a pytest file test_calc.py covering the add and divide functions in calc.py, including division by zero, then run it. Do not use sub-agents.
Review calc.py, strings.py and dates.py for bugs. Launch one sub-agent per file in a single message so they run at the same time, then summarise what they found.
Write a one-paragraph docstring for each of calc.py, strings.py and dates.py. Use three sub-agents launched together, one per file, then report which ones changed.
First use a sub-agent to list which functions in this directory lack tests. When it reports back, use a second sub-agent to write tests for the first function it named. Then run the tests yourself.

Use a sub-agent to find duplicated logic across the python files here. When it answers, use another sub-agent to extract the duplication into a shared helper module. Then check the files still import cleanly.

Launch two sub-agents at once, one to list all TODO comments and one to list all functions longer than 15 lines. When both have reported, use a third sub-agent to write findings.md combining their results.
Launch sub-agents in parallel to summarise calc.py and strings.py. Then, using both summaries, write a README.md for the directory yourself.
Three sub-agents at the same time: one renames the variable `x` in calc.py to something meaningful, one does the same in strings.py, one in dates.py. Report what each renamed.
